baseline_models.focus_anchor: The restrictive construction innama yanhakumu and the linked clauses qatalukum, akhrajukum, and zaharu ala ikhrajikum.
baseline_models.mechanism: The prohibition is keyed to a visible conduct profile: reciprocal fighting in the sphere of din, forced removal, and support for that removal. Nahy as both restraint and endpoint gives the rule a boundary; wala is withheld after that boundary is crossed rather than from an unnamed class in the abstract.

activation_trace.role: Active checking and restraint supplies the operative force of the prohibition.
The sense of an endpoint supplies a lexical edge that reinforces innama as a bounded rule.
Reciprocal combat supplies the first conduct threshold rather than undifferentiated dislike.
An ordered way of obedience supplies the contested sphere of combat without itself becoming the prohibited relation.
Causative bringing-out supplies forced displacement and its repeated nominalized process.
Strength gained through backers makes assistance in displacement part of the operative conduct profile.
Love joined to support supplies the relational alignment withheld from actors meeting that profile.

changed_reading.before: A general ban on friendship with religious outsiders.
changed_reading.after: A delimited ban on giving loving support or alliance to actors whose reciprocal combat, displacement, and assistance in displacement cross the ayah's stated conduct threshold.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The progression from fighting and expelling to zaharu ala ikhrajikum, followed by an tatwallawhum.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah treats violence as enabled, not merely performed. Naming assistance after direct fighting and expulsion makes the relevant object of non-alignment a displacement network whose force can be strengthened by others; wala would add another layer of backing to that same network.

activation_trace.role: Mutual fighting supplies the network's overt violent action.
Causative extraction supplies the network's shared project of displacement.
Backing and reinforcement expose enabling support as part of the harm rather than a neutral edge activity.
Supportive alliance would recruit the addressee into the same chain of reinforcement.
Withholding a due right frames support for the displacement network as participation in deprivation.

changed_reading.before: Only the person who directly attacks or expels is a prohibited ally.
changed_reading.after: The boundary reaches the enabling coalition around displacement, because material or social backing is itself named as an operative part of the aggression.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled forms of w-l-y after removal from diyar and the concluding humu al-zalimun.
baseline_models.mechanism: Wala can organize proximity, care, support, and charge over affairs. Granting that protective position to those who have broken another community's inhabited security puts relational authority in the wrong place and withholds protection from those dispossessed.

activation_trace.role: The resident or householder sense makes diyar an inhabited protection-space rather than incidental scenery.
Causative removal supplies the prior destruction of that protection-space.
Nearness without an intervening gap supplies the intimacy of the reassigned relation.
Taking charge of an affair supplies a jurisdictional layer beyond private liking.
Putting something in the wrong place diagnoses the relocation of protective authority to the agents of dispossession.
Blocking a right supplies the corresponding deprivation suffered by those expelled.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoing is simply feeling friendship toward the wrong people.
changed_reading.after: The wrongdoing is a misallocation of protective proximity and authority: those who stripped a people of inhabited security are installed as its intimates, supporters, or governors.

context_deltas.mechanism: 60:1 decomposes tawalli into deliberate adoption of awliya, casting affection toward them, and maintaining that relation across hidden and declared registers. The focus prohibition therefore concerns an enacted channel of supportive intimacy and communication, not an involuntary residue of warmth.

activation_trace.role: Love and support anchor the focus act that the earlier context operationalizes.
Deliberate acquisition makes enemy-as-wali a constructed relation rather than a passing feeling.
The noun awliya supplies the supportive alliance that recurs as a verb in the focus.
Casting something outward turns affection into a directed transfer toward the hostile party.
Repeated affection supplies the content carried through that directed relation.
Interior concealment supplies a covert register in which the relation can be maintained.
Covering and hiddenness make concealed conduct explicitly inspectable rather than irrelevant.
Open manifestation completes the hidden-to-public range across which the enacted alignment can operate.

structural_cues: 60:1 places awliya beside expulsion, repeats mawadda twice, and contrasts what is concealed with what is made public.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deliberate taking, directed casting, repeated affection, and hidden/public registers; I infer that these acts operationalize tawalli as a channel of relational access and support. A live alternative is that the sequence remains primarily affective and need not imply material assistance in every instance.

changed_reading.before: Tawalli is equivalent to merely liking an enemy.
changed_reading.after: Tawalli is a deliberately maintained and directed relation through which affection, access, and support can be carried, whether covertly or openly.

context_deltas.mechanism: 60:7 leaves room for enmity to be remade into affection, while 60:8 repeats the focus roots under a negated prohibition for those who did not fight or expel and positively opens benevolence and equity. The matched contrast makes conduct, not fixed group essence, control the boundary and leaves the relation temporally revisable.

activation_trace.role: The endpoint sense anchors a bounded focus rule whose limit the adjacent contrast exposes.
Hope for return after depletion supplies a branch-distant but vivid image of relational reversibility.
Causing a thing to become a new state supplies the transition from enmity to affection.
Affection is the positive relation that may emerge after the present hostile state.
Negated restraint establishes that the prohibition does not cover the non-aggressing counterpart.
The same reciprocal-combat branch appears under negation, creating an exact behavioral contrast with the focus.
The same causative-removal branch appears under negation, marking non-displacement as boundary-relevant.
Active connection and beneficence supply a permitted positive relation toward non-aggressors.
Equity supplies the governing mode for dealing with those outside the aggression profile.
Enduring love positively values equitable conduct, preventing the boundary from becoming affective dehumanization.

structural_cues: 60:7 places possible future affection after present enmity.
60:8 is a near mirror of 60:9: it repeats n-h-y, q-t-l, d-y-n, kh-r-j, and d-w-r under negation before naming benevolence and equity.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a possible enemy-to-affection transition and a matched non-fighting/non-expelling contrast; I infer that the focus category is conduct-indexed and can change when conduct changes. A live alternative is that 60:7 promises only an exceptional reconciliation without defining the legal scope, though 60:8 still independently resists an identity-wide ban.

changed_reading.before: The prohibited group carries a permanent identity that excludes warm or just relations.
changed_reading.after: The prohibited alignment is contingent on active aggression; non-aggressors remain objects of benevolence and equity, and even present enmity can later become affection.

context_deltas.mechanism: 60:10 refuses to return tested migrant women to hostile jurisdiction while repeatedly settling expenditure, and 60:11 answers reciprocal loss with an equivalent. Read back into 60:9, non-tawalli can mean refusing a transfer of vulnerable persons or protective authority without turning separation into confiscation or suspension of equitable claims.

activation_trace.role: Forced bringing-out anchors the focus in displaced persons rather than an abstract contest alone.
Charge over affairs supplies the protective-jurisdiction dimension revised by the later settlement.
Movement from one home-domain to another supplies the concrete displaced persons whose status must be decided.
A test that discloses inward commitment makes protection depend on examined status rather than automatic group capture.
Return to the prior condition supplies the transfer explicitly refused for the migrant women.
Money that has gone out supplies the repeatedly balanced property claim alongside the refusal to return persons.
A holding bond that protects and prevents supplies the legal tie that is not to be retained indiscriminately.
Adjudication between parties turns boundary maintenance into an ordered settlement rather than reciprocal seizure.
Replacement and guarantee supply a compensatory response to loss across the boundary.
Equivalence supplies the measure by which the compensatory claim is balanced.

structural_cues: 60:10 tests migrant women, forbids returning them, and repeatedly orders repayment of expenditure.
60:11 answers a reciprocal loss with an equivalent to what was spent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies migration, examination, non-return, severable bonds, repayment, and adjudication; I infer an institutional distinction between jurisdiction over persons and compensable property claims. A live alternative is that this distinction is confined to the marital migration case and should not be generalized to every form of tawalli.

changed_reading.before: Refusing alliance with aggressors requires total severance and suspends obligations across the boundary.
changed_reading.after: The boundary can refuse the return of displaced persons to hostile control while still adjudicating and compensating material claims with measured reciprocity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same q-t-l field appears later as direct killing within a pledged moral catalogue, whereas the focus uses qatalu and activates reciprocal combat before coordinated expulsion. The contrast sharpens 60:9 from a vague association with dangerous people to actual belligerency, while 60:12 locates non-killing inside an accountable covenant.

activation_trace.role: Reciprocal combat anchors the focus criterion in fighting between parties.
Direct taking of life supplies a contrasting q-t-l realization inside the later moral pledge.
A pledge of obedience supplies the accountable communal frame surrounding the prohibition of killing.
Recognized good supplies the normative field in which the pledge is governed rather than an enemy label.

structural_cues: 60:12 places yaqtulna awladahunna inside a repeated bayaa construction, while 60:9 uses qatalukum and joins it to expulsion and assistance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distinct verbal forms, a direct-killing branch in 60:12, and a reciprocal-combat branch in 60:9; I infer that the focus threshold is organized belligerency rather than generic moral danger. A live alternative is that the two uses simply sample a broad violence field without narrowing the social rule as sharply.

changed_reading.before: Any association with people marked by killing or moral danger triggers the focus prohibition.
changed_reading.after: The focus specifically names those who fought the addressees and joined that fighting to displacement, while other lethal wrongdoing is handled within a distinct covenantal frame.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the circular branch of d-w-r beneath diyar and turns the clause into a spatial model. It remains anchored in the focus's home, doubled expulsion, dominance, immediate proximity, and wrong-placement roots. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for protective space, not as the lexical definition of diyar or the sole legal rationale.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Diyari-kum, the repeated kh-r-j forms, zaharu ala, the doubled w-l-y forms, and al-zalimun.

activation_trace.role: Circular enclosure supplies an image of the home as a protective orbit around its inhabitants.
Repeated causative extraction supplies the breach and removal from that orbit.
Ascending dominance places the assisting power above the breached domestic field.
Gapless nearness would reinstall the displacing power at the intimate edge of the damaged enclosure.
Wrong emplacement names the spatial contradiction of admitting the breaching power as nearest protector.

changed_reading.before: Homes are merely locations from which the addressees were expelled.
changed_reading.after: Homes become a breached protective orbit, and tawalli becomes the paradoxical installation of the displacing power in immediate proximity to the enclosure it helped break.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it carries the face-orientation branch of w-l-y and the despair-and-graves sequence of 60:13 back into 60:9, then sets them against 60:7's hope of returned affection. It remains anchored by the repeated tawalli construction and the context's opposed future states. Downstream prose should qualify it as an existential resonance of affiliation, not replace 60:9's explicit aggression criterion with a doctrine about inner despair.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: An tatwallawhum and wa-man yatawallahum, read beside the repeated tawalli prohibition in 60:13.

activation_trace.role: Turning the face toward something supplies an orientational layer within the focus's act of affiliation.
Hope for a depleted good to return supplies an open future against which closed affiliation can be sensed.
Possible affection supplies the future relation that keeps present enmity from becoming an essence.
The repeated prohibition of face-turning links affiliation to adopted orientation in the closing context.
Cut-off hope supplies the closed future horizon associated with that later prohibited orientation.
Burial and concealment of the dead give the closed horizon a terminal material image.

changed_reading.before: Tawalli is only an external political arrangement.
changed_reading.after: Tawalli may also involve borrowing another party's orientation toward the future; the context contrasts an affiliation closed by severed hope with the still-open possibility that enmity becomes affection.

strongest_changes: The focus became a conduct-delimited rule keyed to reciprocal fighting, forced displacement, and assistance in displacement rather than a permanent identity ban.
Tawalli expanded from generic friendship into a deliberately maintained channel of loving support, proximity, and potentially protective authority.
60:7-8 kept future affection open and required benevolence and equity toward those outside the aggression profile.
60:10-11 exposed an institutional asymmetry: persons need not be returned to hostile control even while material claims remain measurable and compensable.
summary.what_was_special: The most productive activation was the coexistence of social, legal, spatial, and temporal readings without collapsing them: coalition support can trigger the boundary, justice still crosses it, domestic space can image what was violated, and the relation remains reversible when conduct changes.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus alone does not fully settle how much w-l-y here weights affection, practical support, alliance, or jurisdiction.
The aggression clauses may describe one cumulatively qualified cohort or a coalition-level pattern whose enabling roles are distributed.
The person/property distinction in 60:10-11 may be specific to the migration and marital settlement rather than a general rule for every boundary conflict.
The breached-orbit and borrowed-horizon readings remain analogical activations and should not displace the explicit conduct criterion.
